questions: If a folder is absent when checked but a concurrent call creates it before this call's creation attempt, must the losing call re-check and accept the folder, or must its failed exclusive creation fail the write?

When another call creates the folder after this call observes it absent but before this call creates it, must an already-exists result be followed by a safe recheck and acceptance, or is it a failed creation that fails the write?

When two calls both observe a folder as missing and one creates it before the other's creation attempt, must the losing call treat the already-created folder as success after rechecking it, or treat its failed creation call as a failed write?

quotes:
The service makes the folders below the binary store and the state folder exist one at a time, from
   the outermost: a folder it finds is accepted, whoever created it, also a concurrent call, when it is a
   folder; a missing one is created with the mode of the imported `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the
   binary store and of the imported `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constant in the state folder, set whatever the
   process umask. In the binary store the folders are those of the path resolved under rule 1. In the state
   folder an entry on the way that is a symbolic link or not a folder fails the write, and a failure to
   create a folder or set its mode fails it too; for the lock file that is the refusal of rule 5.
judgement.divergence: After an already-exists result caused by a concurrent creator, one implementation safely rechecks and accepts the folder while another treats the creation attempt as failed; the operation's caller observes continuation versus failure or STATE_UNAVAILABLE.
judgement.why: The rule permits accepting a folder created by a concurrent call and also says a failed creation fails the write, without deciding which applies when creation loses an absent-to-present race.

topics.topic: Publication-mark timestamp authority, sampling event, clock-read count, and datetime representation
questions: Which authority supplies the fresh instant written to `marked_at`?

At which event is `marked_at` sampled, and how many clock readings may one mark operation take—on request receipt, before waiting for the project lock, after taking the lock, immediately before writing, or after the rename?
What exact representation must every written or compared instant use, including timezone awareness, UTC normalization, JSON spelling, fractional-second precision and comparison precision?
What clock supplies a new publication mark's `marked_at`, in what datetime representation is it stored, and exactly how many clock readings may one mark operation take?

quotes:
The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
judgement.why: A7 identifies the clock authority, fixes the single sampling point and read count, and specifies the exact UTC-naive microsecond representation and serialization.

questions: Does the exception for the project lock also permit A6 to create and permanently retain the lock file's missing parent folders before a delivery later fails condition 1 to 4?

quotes:
Conditions 1 to 4 write nothing except the
   project lock.

A folder the
   service has created stays: it is never removed, also when the write it was created for fails.

topics.topic: Conversion of camera-local timestamps without UTC offsets
questions: When a camera record contains a local date and time but no UTC offset, how is it converted to the required UTC instant?

quotes:
The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM` with hours up to 14 and minutes up to 59; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`.

The photo date is delivered as UTC without an offset, as the Client Portal stores it. A camera
   time with no offset is read in the configured time zone. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
judgement.why: A2 says offsetless camera values use the configured time zone and specifies ambiguous and nonexistent local-time handling before conversion to UTC without an offset.

quotes:

   failure of the operation; only its survival of a host crash is uncertain.
judgement.why: A6 expressly makes a post-rename containing-folder synchronization failure non-fatal for both placement and mark records.

topics.topic: Whether damaged-record tests must prove that no new durable artifacts were created
questions: For every damaged-record case, must the tests also show that no new placement record, mark record or stored image was created, rather than showing only the refusal and preservation of the damaged record?

quotes: - INV-20: a damaged record never leads to a new placement or a new mark.

- INV-20: with a damaged placement or mark record, scan, delivery and mark each answer M08 with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode and the record stays as it was (`test_a_damaged_record_refuses_and_is_never_taken_for_an_absent_one`), a damaged mark without a placement stops a new placement (`test_a_damaged_mark_without_a_placement_stops_a_new_placement`), a mark that cannot be written is refused (`test_a_mark_that_cannot_be_written_is_refused`), and a record that is a link, dangling or not, or that names another source is refused the same way (`test_a_record_not_written_at_its_address_is_refused`).

A record that is a link, even a dangling one, or that
   cannot be opened or read, is not valid JSON, fails that validation or names another project or source
   is never taken for an absent record: the operation is refused with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode, whose value is
   `state_unavailable`, and changes no record and no stored image.
judgement.divergence: One required-test implementation checks only the refusal and preservation of the damaged record, while another also verifies that no placement record, mark record or stored image was created; the test suite can accept different durable side effects.
judgement.why: The Required tests item does not require every damaged-record case to demonstrate the normative no-new-record and no-new-image effects.

topics.topic: Whether lock files follow the ordinary atomic file-write protocol
questions: Does “Each file” include the lock file, or are lock files created and opened directly under rule 4 without the temporary-write, rename and folder-synchronisation protocol?

quotes:
Each file is written to a temporary name in its folder, synchronised to disk and renamed, and
